title: Footnotes & Margins
desc: The people history forgot, inventions credited to the wrong person & accidental empires

questions.q: Who actually invented the lightbulb — because it wasn't just Edison?
questions.a: At least 20 inventors worked on incandescent lighting before Edison. Humphry Davy, Warren de la Rue, and Joseph Swan all had working versions. Edison perfected the commercially viable one

questions.q: Hedy Lamarr was a 1940s Hollywood star who also co-invented what foundational technology?
questions.a: Frequency-hopping spread spectrum — the basis for modern Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS

questions.q: The Phlogiston Theory dominated chemistry for over a century. What was it and why was it wrong?
questions.a: It claimed combustible materials contained 'phlogiston' that was released during burning. Lavoisier disproved it by demonstrating that combustion requires oxygen

questions.q: Which country had a female pharaoh, warrior queens, and a written language before most of Europe?
questions.a: The Kingdom of Kush (modern-day Sudan) — with Kandakes (warrior queens) and Meroitic script

questions.q: The Treaty of Tordesillas in 1494 did what extraordinary thing?
questions.a: Split the entire non-Christian world between Spain and Portugal — drawing a line through the Atlantic. That's why Brazil speaks Portuguese

questions.q: Ada Lovelace is credited as the first computer programmer. What machine was she writing for?
questions.a: Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine — a mechanical general-purpose computer that was never fully built

questions.q: What was 'Greek fire' and why was it so feared?
questions.a: A Byzantine incendiary weapon that burned on water and couldn't be extinguished. The exact formula was a state secret and has been lost to history

questions.q: The 'Year Without a Summer' (1816) was caused by what?
questions.a: The eruption of Mount Tambora in Indonesia in 1815 — volcanic ash blocked sunlight globally, causing crop failures, snow in June, and famine

questions.q: Who were the Harlem Hellfighters and why were they significant?
questions.a: The 369th Infantry Regiment — an African-American unit in WWI that spent 191 days in combat (the longest of any American unit) and never lost a trench. France awarded them the Croix de Guerre; America largely ignored them

questions.q: Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital, was larger than any European city when the Spanish arrived. What modern city sits on its ruins?
